query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve dynamic strength–ductility performance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an untreated baseline, defines the boundary conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a specific grain refinement through severe plastic deformation can improve dynamic strength-ductility performance in high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys with coarse grain structure
generation.mechanism: Grain boundary strengthening and enhanced dislocation density
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved strength and ductility compared to untreated baseline
generation.boundary: Applicable to alloys with specific compositions and processing histories
generation.uncertainty: Influence of deformation routes and resulting microstructures on dynamic properties

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of dynamic mechanical properties between severely plastically deformed and undeformed high-entropy alloy samples
measurements: Tensile testing at high strain rates
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: No significant improvement in strength-ductility performance in deformed samples compared to undeformed ones
